## Overview

X released an expanded open-source version of the code that powers its "For You" feed on August 13, 2026, publishing it to a new GitHub repository under the Apache License 2.0, according to [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/13/x-open-sources-its-ranking-algorithm-letting-users-see-if-theyve-been-shadowbanned/) and the repository itself on [GitHub](https://github.com/xai-org/x-algorithm). editor_notes.content_quality: Well-organized News piece that handles a genuine cross-source discrepancy (TechCrunch's 'Grok' vs. the repo's 'Grox') correctly by reporting each in its own source's language and flagging the unresolved discrepancy in 'What We Don't Know' rather than silently harmonizing them.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both snapshots directly. TechCrunch confirms the '10 to 15 times larger' quote, the Under-the-Hood tool's eligibility criteria and pilot-rollout details, the Keith Coleman 'run yourself outside the company' quote, and the Grok-exclusion rationale verbatim. Notably, TechCrunch's 'fairly shocked' Coleman quote does check out verbatim in the snapshot, but the article correctly doesn't use it -- consistent with the write-agent's own report that it dropped an unconfirmable quote out of caution; the caution held even where the quote turned out to be accurate. The GitHub repo confirms the self-description, the Phoenix/Thunder/SimClusters system names, the withheld-files rationale quote, and the Grox table-row description ('Runs as posts are published. Classifiers for categories such as spam, adult content and violent media...') verbatim.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specifics trace verbatim to their cited sources. No hallucinations or misattributions found.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout; the Analysis section is framed as analysis and doesn't take Coleman's 'verifiable' framing at face value.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate -- no prior archive coverage of X's ranking-algorithm open-source releases.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Approve. Every quote and specific verified verbatim across both sources; the Grok/Grox naming discrepancy is handled correctly by disclosure rather than false harmonization. No corrections needed.
